title: Implicit intersection (@) and legacy array formulas

cases.note: A pre-dynamic-array formula =A1:A5 in row 2 takes the value from row 2 (implicit intersection). Excel 365 shows it as =@A1:A5.
In a row outside the range there is nothing to intersect: #VALUE!.
The @ operator does implicit intersection explicitly.
The same formula entered as a dynamic-array formula spills all five values.
Implicit intersection also works across columns: =D1:H1 in column F takes F1.
SUM(A*B) entered the old way, without Ctrl+Shift+Enter: Excel 365 may add @ and give a different result than the array version.
The same formula entered with Ctrl+Shift+Enter (FormulaArray) multiplies element by element: 10+40+90.
A legacy multi-cell array formula fills exactly the selected range.
A legacy array formula entered into more cells than the result has fills the extra cells with #N/A.
@ on an array returned by a function takes its first element.
@ on a single cell changes nothing.
INDEX(range,0) returns the whole column; entered the old way it is intersected with the formula's row.
IF(A1:A5>25,...) entered the old way tests only the value in the formula's row.
A whole-column reference entered the old way intersects with the formula's row.
